title: Evidence Attribution in Visual Document Understanding without Coordinates or Region Labels
hook: With a language-cue interface, we find the grounding bottleneck is the coordinate output, not the model's ability to locate the evidence.

title: IKEA-Bench: Benchmarking and Mechanistic Analysis of Vision-Language Models for Cross-Depiction Assembly Instruction Alignment
hook: Can a VLM match an abstract IKEA diagram to a video of the real build? Text is a double-edged sword — it recovers instruction understanding but silently breaks diagram-to-video alignment, and scaling up won't help: the visual encoder is the real bottleneck.

title: NanoVDR: Distilling a 2B Vision-Language Retriever into a 70M Text-Only Encoder for Visual Document Retrieval
hook: What if your query encoder didn't need to see at all? 2B → 70M, 95% quality, 50× faster.

title: DistilVDR: A Compact End-to-End Visual Document Retriever via Dual-Student Distillation
hook: NanoVDR shrank only the query encoder. DistilVDR distills the whole retriever end-to-end from a single 8B teacher, keeping most of its quality at 524M with a 15x smaller index.

title: Structural Anchor Pruning: Training-Free Multi-Vector Compression for Visual Document Retrieval
hook: Where does a document's structure actually live in a VLM? Wherever it is, SAP finds it — and prunes 90% of multi-vector indexes, training-free.

title: Exploring Human-AI Collaboration in E-Textile Design: A Case Study on Flex Sensor Placement for Shoulder Motion Detection
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction, 2026
hook: Does LLM-assisted design always help humans? Junior designers gain from human-AI collaboration; experienced ones regress.

title: Encoder-Free Human Motion Understanding via Structured Motion Descriptions
hook: What if motion didn't need an encoder at all? Just describe it in words — and let the LLM reason.

title: Fine-grained Motion Retrieval via Joint-Angle Motion Images and Token-Patch Late Interaction
hook: Turn a 3D skeleton into a pseudo-image, then retrieve it like a document — with token-level explainability.

title: LingoMotion: An Interpretable and Unambiguous Symbolic Representation for Human Motion
venue: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications (PerCom) Work-in-Progress, 2026
hook: What if human motion had its own alphabet, words, and grammar — just like natural language?
